messages:
Maya: heads-up: deploy-bot is flagging increased error-rate and p95 on the embeddings pipeline right after v3.1.0 rollout to eu-west-1. auto-action suggests fallback to stable or full rollback. tagging @Raj and @Jules for quick decision.

deploy-bot: DEPLOYBOT ALERT — embeddings-service eu-west-1: error_rate +12% and p95_latency +28% vs baseline in the last 10m. Suggested mitigations: 1) traffic-slice to model=v3-stable (recommended) 2) manual rollback to v3.0.7 (if error persists). Confidence: medium-high. Telemetry: https://telemetry/redwood/embeddings/eu-west-1

Raj: looking at logs, we have a spike of OOM-ish retries in the new quant matmul path when sequences exceed 2048 tokens. Not hitting node OOMs, but retries cause tail latency. Also seeing a small increase in tokenization mismatch for certain non-latin inputs.

Jules: fwiw, v3.1.0 enabled aggressive kv-eviction for memory headroom on trimmed hosts. That change could explain tail effects on long-context requests. Rollback would revert eviction policy.

Maya: ops question: any impacted dedicated customers pinned to v3.1.0? We should avoid touching pinned pools if possible.

ops-runner: quick check: two dedicated pools in eu-west-1 are on v3.1.0; they cannot be transparently rerouted without customer consent. If we rollback globally, dedicated pools will be affected. We can do a scoped traffic-slice on the region's hosted routes only.

Raj: my vote is for a scoped fallback to v3-stable for hosted traffic in eu-west-1 for 20m while eng-ml investigates. That buys us time and avoids global rollback.

Jules: agree. command for ops:

```sh
redwood route update --service embeddings-service --region eu-west-1 --target-model v3-stable --scope hosted --percent 100 --ttl 20m --reason "p95+err mitigation"
```

This keeps dedicated pools untouched and is reversible.

Elena: comms note: even for a temporary fallback we should add a console banner and an internal incident note. If we rollback, we need an email template and change-log revision. I'll prepare both but hold sending until decision.

Maya: who signs off? For scoped route we need ops + oncall (Raj). For full rollback: eng-release + product + ops.

Raj: oncall approves scoped route. ops-runner you have green to execute.

ops-runner: executing route update now. RunID: rt-3267890123-01. Marking as non-rollback (fallback) action.

deploy-bot: ACTION LOG — route update applied: service=embeddings-service region=eu-west-1 scope=hosted target_model=v3-stable percent=100 ttl=20m. RunID=rt-3267890123-01

ops-runner: done. watching for metric changes.

Raj: metrics trending down within 2m. error-rate back to baseline, p95 improved ~20%. No change in dedicated pools (expected).

Jules: starting a targeted repro matrix for long-context non-latin prompts against v3.1.0 in canary infra. I'll post findings in 15m.

Elena: publishing internal incident note and adding console banner: "Temporary mitigation applied for embeddings v3.1.0 in eu-west-1; hosted traffic routed to v3-stable while we investigate. Expected follow-up within 2 hours." Customer-facing email draft ready but not sent.

Maya: action items captured: (1) eng-ml (Jules/Raj) to root-cause eviction/retry behavior (2) ops to hold the fallback for 20m and extend if needed (3) Elena to prepare comms and escalate to CS for dedicated customers if rollback becomes necessary.

Raj: reproducible case found in canary with kv-eviction threshold + quant matmul on 3x batch long sequences. PR in flight to reduce eviction aggressiveness and add a safety-check.

Maya: good. keep the fallback unless regressions reappear. If PR fixes things and metrics stay stable for a 1h window, we'll re-allow v3.1.0 traffic. If not, we'll schedule a controlled rollback with release notes and customer communications.

ops-runner: marking rt-3267890123-01 as live. ping ops-runner for manual rollback runbook if we need to escalate. :white_check_mark:

Maya: thanks team. will update after 20m window or earlier if anything changes.
